title: Skillify
lede: How finished work becomes a reusable skill that every agent and every downstream repo can invoke.

context.name: Reconstruct context
context.role: Rebuild what the session did without asking the user to re-explain.
details: Reads the conversation, project manifests, git diff --stat and git log.
Writes a one-paragraph recap that the user confirms in one line.

interview.name: Interview
interview.role: Four short rounds, one question at a time, each with a recommended answer.
details: Intent, then inputs, then steps, then edge cases.
Stops early if all four are already clear from context.

name.name: Name and dedupe
name.role: Pick one skill, give it a short name, and check it isn't a duplicate.
details: One skill per run: if the session had several, pick the most valuable and say so.
The slug is kebab-case, at most 30 characters, and stated before any file is written.
risks: If RESOLVER already has a skill with overlapping purpose, extend that one with an argument instead of adding a near-duplicate.
qs: Why only one skill per run?

generate.name: Generate and register
generate.role: Write the skill body and its wrappers, register it, and validate.

more: Thin wrappers for Claude, Cursor, .agents and .agent/workflows point at it, all with the same description.
A RESOLVER row with a unique ^/slug anchor.
New paths appended to .github/scaffold-files.txt so sync copies them.
A focused test for any script logic.

risks: Register or it doesn't ship: client discovery alone does not make a skill available through scaffold sync.
node scripts/check-resolvable.ts must pass before the PR; it rejects wrapper descriptions that drift apart.

upstream.name: PR to scaffold
upstream.role: Open a pull request against scaffold so every repo inherits the skill, then stop for review.
details: Branch `skillify/<slug>` off `scaffold/main`, push, and open a PR titled `feat(skill): <slug>`.
Do not merge; the summary lists slug, files, validator result and PR link.

slug.d: The skill's short kebab-case name, used everywhere it is referenced.

resolver.d: The routing table that maps /slug to its skill file.

wrapper.d: A thin per-tool file that points at the canonical skill body.

ask.context: The reader wants to understand scaffold's /skillify skill: how an AI agent turns a finished session into a registered, reusable skill.
